articles.title: From Playground to Caching: Learning Amazon Bedrock
articles.excerpt: This post is part of my notes from Formação AWS, a course by Henrylle Maia. It covers a class from Desafio Labs (one of the course's sections) that focuses on Amazon Bedrock. In this class, I start wi…
articles.body: This post is part of my notes from Formação AWS , a course by Henrylle Maia. It covers a class from Desafio Labs (one of the course's sections) that focuses on Amazon Bedrock. In this class, I start with the Playground to get a feel for how Bedrock behaves, and then move on to scripts to learn how to actually use the Bedrock API. To learn by doing, I created a simple chatbot that works like a clerk selling tickets for an AWS Course. It starts as a single Bash script that sends one message and prints the response, then I make it interactive so I can actually chat with it. From there, I move it to Node so I can stream the answers as they come in, and finally add a cache checkpoint so the same System Prompt doesn't get billed at full price on every message.

articles.title: How to Reuse an Existing TON Connect Instance with Omniston Widget Integrated Mode
articles.excerpt: If your TON dApp already has wallet connectivity, you should not create another TON Connect instance just for the Omniston Widget. Instead, configure the widget in integrated mode and pass it the same…
articles.body: If your TON dApp already has wallet connectivity, you should not create another TON Connect instance just for the Omniston Widget. Instead, configure the widget in integrated mode and pass it the same initialized instance that the rest of your application already uses. The result is one shared wallet session across your interface. A wallet connected through your navigation, account panel, or another TON feature can also be used by the embedded Omniston swap interface. More importantly, this follows the architecture required by the current STON.fi widget integration, which warns against running multiple TON Connect instances inside the same application. Why reuse the connection instead of creating another one? Imagine a TON dashboard that already has a wallet button in its header.

The 1994 action-adventure movie with a sci-fi twist drops Egyptologist Daniel Jackson (James Spader) and Special Forces Colonel Jack O'Neil (Kurt Russell) into an otherworldly Egypt after unlocking a portal that allows access across the universe. articles.excerpt: Metaphor ReFantazio has a lot in common with Fortune's Weave, like calendar management, world map exploration, and a reputation mechanic
articles.body: There have been plenty of RPGs over the years that include an arena combat segment. It's as much a staple of the genre as a sewer dungeon and a prison break. But most of the time, it's just a brief diversion from the main quest of saving the world and/or killing a wrathful god. That's not the case with Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave , whose first act lets you experience Dagsion's Heroic Games through the eyes of four rival contenders . If you're enchanted by the concept of an RPG centered around a high-stakes tournament, you absolutely need to check out Atlus's 2024 banger, Metaphor ReFantazio .

articles.excerpt: Lanterns regains its lost momentum in Episode 7, as the show reconnects with the core Hal/John dynamic we love so much. Read our full review.
articles.body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 7! The worst part about Lanterns finally diving into the 2026 storyline first teased back in the pilot is that it forces us into a post-Hal Jordan reality. So much of the appeal of the series rests on the sour dynamic between Kyle Chandler's Hal and Aaron Pierre's John Stewart, and there's just something missing without the former in play. Thankfully, there's a workaround in the form of the Halogram backup. Episode 7 exploits that loophole for all its worth, resulting in a new installment that digs far deeper into Hal's troubled psyche and dark family legacy. Fittingly, this week kicks off with a flashback to Hal's childhood, where we finally meet Martin Jordan (Jake B. Miller) in the flesh.

articles.title: NASA Tests Dual Mode Propulsion CubeSat Ahead of Launch
articles.excerpt: Spacecraft propulsion traditionally relies on volatile fuels and separate, bulky systems for different types of maneuvering in space. NASA is working to change that paradigm. Engineers at NASA’s Marsh…
articles.body: Spacecraft propulsion traditionally relies on volatile fuels and separate, bulky systems for different types of maneuvering in space. NASA is working to change that paradigm. Engineers at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, recently completed a rigorous series of environmental and physical tests on a new small satellite designed to make spaceflight safer and more efficient. The ASCENT (Advanced Spacecraft Energetic Non-Toxic) Propulsion Dual Mode mission is a flight demonstration of a spacecraft about the size of a large shoebox.
